findings: Four original-JavaScript controls confirm ambiguous completion and delayed-start behavior: Stop before POST response opens SSE later; SSE error shows complete/100%; rejected fetch overwrites error with complete; server error leaves Search hidden.
Global eventSource is shared across runs and asynchronous callbacks lack a generation token. No broad concurrency claim: the specific delayed-response case is controlled.
Cache scan UI distinguishes connection interruption from completion, unlike image search UI.
UI accepts image/* but discovery is JPEG-only, and upload decoding is limited by Go decoder registration; MIME acceptance is not format coverage.
EXIF GPS display uses truthiness of latitude and longitude; valid zero coordinates are omitted by source inspection.
Directory loads have no response-generation guard; cached directory count labels image versions as images. Source observations, not runtime controls.
remaining: template.html whole-read and UI render review
limits: Minimal DOM/fetch/EventSource adapters, no real browser or HTTP server.
No production code adoption; native pHash/ASAN remains deferred.
